newsitem.title: UK: French truck ban to cost UK firms 27 mln stg/year.
newsitem.headline: French truck ban to cost UK firms 27 mln stg/year.

text.p: The weekend lorry ban in France due to come into force on March 24 will cost British business up to 27 million sterling a year, the Freight Transport Association (FTA) said.

The Easter weekend will be a particularly difficult one for British lorry drivers returning to the UK as there is also a lorry ban in operation in France on the Monday after Easter causing a 48 hour interruption to journeys, the FTA said.

This is the first time that overseas drivers returning home have been included in the French lorry ban. Instead they will have to park up and sit around for a complete day from 10 pm every Saturday, the FTA said a statement.
However, exemptions remain for carriers of certain products such as fresh produce, live animals and seasonal produce.

It estimated that the extension of the French ban to foreign lorries will affect at least some 2,500 British lorries every week. The fixed cost for a lorry and driver is at least 180 stg a day. With overtime payments and restrictions on working hours, the real costs may be much higher.

The FTA said many hauliers will attempt to reschedule deliveries and collections around the new disruption, but because of lorry bans in other countries and modern production cycles, not everyone will be able to do this.
In the worst cases, companies will have to buy extra lorries simply to meet existing contracts, which could in turn impact efficiency, it added.
The FTA said many British firms are becoming increasingly frustrated with the slowness of the French compensation scheme for the French truckers' strike last November.
There are also persistent suggestions of possible further blockades in France and Spain are causing further concern to British hauliers and shippers, it added.

The European Commission has yet to make any suggestions as to how freight carried by road can be protected against future action by single pressure groups, the FTA said. ((- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017))
